correctness.rationale: Every extension-generated cube is terminal and has constituent-block length in {1,2,3,4}; no two letters share a length. Explicit Parikh contradictions exclude all witness triples containing 3, forcing {1,2,4}. Relabeling yields 12 choices for first block, 4 for middle block, fixed suffix 100; only four candidates contain a cube. All 44 remaining representatives have three terminal witness cubes and unique normalization, hence 264 labeled words. The standalone checker independently enumerates all 3^11=177,147 words, confirms exactly 50,520 avoid cubes, identifies exactly 264 crucial words and 44 permutation classes, and verifies none at lengths below 11. No infinite claim rests merely on finite experiments.

value.rationale: The previously known shortest length 11 makes its complete extremizer spectrum a natural exact invariant. The theorem determines not just a count, but a unique 44-representative normal form, four obstructions, the exact action of the six alphabet permutations, and a forced extension-period mechanism. It resolves the full shortest ternary case rather than an arbitrary subset or a routine restatement of the shortest-length theorem. No larger-length or general-alphabet significance is assumed.
